intro: Requests Meridian is likely to make. Each one leaves the blueprint. Decide each card and watch what the project carries.
punchline: This is how a client ends up with a system designed for them instead of to best practice.

riskLevels.label: On blueprint
riskLevels.description: Standard process. Upgrades and testing stay routine.

riskLevels.label: Contained
riskLevels.description: A few deliberate exceptions, each with an owner.

riskLevels.label: Elevated
riskLevels.description: Exceptions start to shape the design and the test plan.

riskLevels.label: High
riskLevels.description: Every release now needs regression work on custom code.

riskLevels.label: Severe
riskLevels.description: The system is designed around legacy habit. Upgrades become projects.

requests.request: Rebuild our legacy dispatch board exactly as it looks today.
requests.context: Dispatchers have used the same screen for years and fear losing speed.
requests.blueprintAlternative: Use the standard schedule board with saved views per branch. Configure filters and columns; do not rebuild the screen.
requests.ongoingDetail: A custom board must be retested and often reworked with every platform release.
askWhy: What can a dispatcher do on the old board in one click that worries them most?
Which information on the old board is used every hour, and which is habit?
If the standard board showed at-risk jobs first, would the layout still matter?

requests.request: We need custom pricing rules per technician.
requests.context: Senior technicians have historically charged higher rates at some branches.
requests.blueprintAlternative: Price by contract, price list, and labor role. Technician rates belong in cost, not in the price the customer sees.
requests.ongoingDetail: Custom pricing logic has to be retested whenever price lists or contracts change.
askWhy: Is the customer paying for the technician, or for the skill the job needs?
Would a labor role such as senior or specialist capture the same rule?
Who approves a rate today, and is that written down?

requests.request: Keep the separate warranty tool and integrate it.
requests.context: The warranty team is comfortable with its tool and worries about migration.
requests.blueprintAlternative: Model warranty as an entitlement on the asset and agreement in the platform, and retire the separate tool.
requests.ongoingDetail: Two systems of record for coverage, an interface to monitor, and a second vendor to upgrade against.
askWhy: What does the warranty tool do that an entitlement on the asset would not?
When the two systems disagree about coverage, which one wins?
Is the concern the tool itself, or the history inside it?

requests.request: Build a bespoke report for every branch manager.
requests.context: Each branch manager keeps their own spreadsheet and trusts it.
requests.blueprintAlternative: One branch-performance dashboard built on the blueprint KPIs, filtered by branch.
requests.ongoingDetail: Every bespoke report is a separate definition of margin to maintain and reconcile.
askWhy: Which decisions does each manager make from their spreadsheet?
If every branch saw the same KPIs, what would be missing?
Should branches be compared with each other on the same definitions?

requests.request: Skip entitlement checks for our top accounts.
requests.context: Account managers do not want key customers questioned about coverage.
requests.blueprintAlternative: Give top accounts a premium entitlement tier. The check still runs, and goodwill is recorded rather than invisible.
requests.ongoingDetail: Cheap to build, expensive to carry: leakage on the largest contracts, and no record of what was given away.
askWhy: Is the goal to avoid friction on the call, or to give free work?
Would an automatic premium tier remove the friction without losing the record?
Who decides the list of top accounts, and how often does it change?

requests.request: Let technicians close jobs without logging parts. We will reconcile monthly.
requests.context: Technicians say recording parts on mobile slows them down.
requests.blueprintAlternative: Require parts on the work order before completion, with van stock suggested so recording takes seconds.
requests.ongoingDetail: Keeps Meridian's unbilled-parts problem alive and adds a monthly reconciliation to support.
askWhy: How much of the delay is the app, and how much is finding the part number?
What happens to billing for parts that never get reconciled?
Would a scan or pick-from-van-stock option change the answer?
